report: Reviewed the complete recovery_completeness claim, its sole implementation association in sage_meta::todo, and its sole annotated test, sage_meta::todo::modules_parse_recovery_completeness. Requirements are: (1) an error item or error CST node is terminal for the current parse; (2) recovery must not turn an absent represented member into a conclusive negative; (3) every exhaustive consumer must treat the surrounding set as incomplete; (4) completeness may be recovered only with proof that the error is irrelevant to that particular question. The implementation entry is explicitly TODO: retained parse errors do not yet provide a uniform question-sensitive completeness result. This is a justified existing deferral of the cross-consumer completeness contract, not ordinary implementation evidence. It accounts for both error representations, the propagation obligation, and the relevance qualification as outstanding work; the comment about retained errors is not independent proof of terminal recovery behavior. The complete associated test is also explicitly TODO, contains no assertions, and specifies malformed and unsupported-item fixtures retaining safe sibling symbols while exhaustive consumers reject false negatives from missing constructs. It supplies no behavioral coverage, including no evidence for terminal error CST handling or relevance proofs. Its prerequisite is implementation of question-sensitive completeness propagation from parse recovery to exhaustive consumers; the eventual matrix must include error items and CST nodes, empty and nonempty represented sets, safe sibling retention, and relevant versus provably irrelevant errors. All of those aspects remain visibly deferred under the sole TODO implementation/test pair. No N/A or ordinary implementation/test entries are present. The existing TODO is honest and sufficiently identifies the missing mechanism and follow-up verification, so no evidence edits are required to accept the deferral. Source assessment used the captured claim, full semantic_spec.rs context and selected test, and the captured review policy; no production-code correctness is asserted. Commands executed were cargo meta review start and cargo meta review read; no behavioral tests were executed, and passing this assertion-free placeholder would not validate the guarantee.
